findings.highlight: "Pretty much all of the articles are either about how profitable it was, or they're written by people who saw Touma Kazusa play for the first time. Actual music critics on the other hand…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「ほとんどの記事が、当日の盛況ぶりとか、
冬馬かずさを初めて見た感想とかばかりで、
実際に演奏をきっちりレビューしてるのは…」
findings.explanation: Articles report the concert's lively success and first impressions of Kazusa; the English calls it profitable and partially recasts the article subjects — The contrast between publicity coverage and serious musical criticism survives.
findings.japanese:
「ほとんどの記事が、当日の盛況ぶりとか、
冬馬かずさを初めて見た感想とかばかりで、
実際に演奏をきっちりレビューしてるのは…」
findings.todokanai: "Pretty much all of the articles are either about how profitable it was, or they're written by people who saw Touma Kazusa play for the first time. Actual music critics on the other hand…"

findings.highlight: She carries the air of someone at the top, but her actual skill is far behind.
findings.evidenceJa: 『高い技術で表面上は取り繕っているが、表現力が追いついてきていない』
findings.explanation: The critic says Kazusa uses high technical skill to paper over the surface, while her expressive power has not caught up. The English says her apparent eminence masks deficient actual skill, reversing technique and expression—the very distinction Haruki analyzes afterward.
findings.japanese:
『高い技術で表面上は取り繕っているが、
表現力が追いついてきていない』
findings.todokanai: "She carries the air of someone at the top, but her actual skill is far behind."

findings.highlight: I sincerely wish that this doesn't affect her reputation, and that she doesn't become known as not a 'trendy singer,' but a 'trendy pianist.'
findings.evidenceJa: 『このまま世間での評判に流されて、“流行歌手”ならぬ“流行ピアニスト”のままで終わらないことを切に願う』
findings.explanation: The critic hopes Kazusa will not be swept along by public acclaim and end her career as a mere 'pop-fashion pianist,' a play on 流行歌手. The English instead hopes the review will not affect her reputation and produces a logically broken 'not a trendy singer, but a trendy pianist' construction.
findings.japanese:
『このまま世間での評判に流されて、
“流行歌手”ならぬ“流行ピアニスト”のままで
終わらないことを切に願う』
findings.todokanai: "I sincerely wish that this doesn't affect her reputation, and that she doesn't become known as not a 'trendy singer,' but a 'trendy pianist.'"

findings.highlight: there'll be a change in attitude in the next special edition magazine
findings.evidenceJa: 今回の特集にとっては、少し逆風が吹いたかもしれないな
findings.explanation: Hamada says the negative review may have created a headwind for their current feature on Kazusa. The English invents a future attitude change in the next special-edition magazine, changing both the affected project and the timing.
findings.japanese:
「今のところ編集長から何も言ってきてないが、
今回の特集にとっては、
少し逆風が吹いたかもしれないな」
findings.todokanai: "The chief editor hasn't said anything yet, but I'm willing to bet there'll be a change in attitude in the next special edition magazine."

findings.evidenceJa: 結局、やっと掴んだと思った蜘蛛の糸は、手元からあっさりと断ち切られてしまったから。
findings.explanation: Haruki explicitly calls his fragile lead 蜘蛛の糸, invoking Akutagawa's The Spider's Thread before it snaps in his hands. The English replaces the named image with the generic phrase 'thread of hope,' erasing the literary allusion and its moral/desperate overtones.
findings.japanese:
結局、やっと掴んだと思った蜘蛛の糸は、
手元からあっさりと断ち切られてしまったから。
findings.todokanai: In the end, the moment I thought I'd finally gotten a hold of a thread of hope, it ended up snapping easily in my hands.

findings.evidenceJa: そして、その俺の余裕のなさは、望まない形で正しく報われてしまう。
findings.explanation: It is Haruki's desperate lack of composure—the urgency that drove him to trespass—that is vindicated in the worst possible way when he finds the broken window and blood. The English calls this abstract reasoning being proven right, removing the causal payoff to his reckless emotional state.
findings.japanese:
そして、その俺の余裕のなさは、
望まない形で正しく報われてしまう。
findings.todokanai: And then, my reasoning was proven right in a way I never wanted it to be.

findings.highlight: Even though her mind is in a haze, she certainly didn't mistake me for some unknown intruder.
findings.evidenceJa:
それは、意識が朦朧としてるからでも、
俺を見知らぬ暴漢と間違えた訳でもなかった。
findings.explanation: Kazusa's strike is not because her mind is hazy and not because she mistook him; the English concedes that her mind is in a haze before excluding only mistaken identity — Her subsequent direct accusations establish that the assault is conscious and aimed at Haruki.
findings.japanese:
それは、意識が朦朧としてるからでも、
俺を見知らぬ暴漢と間違えた訳でもなかった。
findings.todokanai: Even though her mind is in a haze, she certainly didn't mistake me for some unknown intruder.

findings.highlight: Reality can't possibly be different from that.
findings.evidenceJa: 現実は、それとは違うだなんて。
findings.explanation: Kazusa dreamed of eventually hating and forgetting Haruki, but reality has turned out differently: she still loves him. The English says reality cannot possibly differ from that imagined future, reversing the contrast that her confession immediately demonstrates.
findings.japanese: 現実は、それとは違うだなんて。
findings.todokanai: Reality can't possibly be different from that.

findings.highlight: You let me go for five whole years!
findings.evidenceJa: 「五年も離れてた！今さらなに言ってんだよ！」
findings.explanation: Haruki says simply that they were apart for five years, challenging Kazusa's plea not to separate now. The English makes Kazusa the person who let him go, inventing unilateral agency and blame in a separation for which Haruki is elsewhere indicting himself.
findings.japanese:
「五年も離れてた！
今さらなに言ってんだよ！」
findings.todokanai: "You let me go for five whole years! What are you saying after all this time?"

findings.highlight: "It doesn't matter if you don't want to, or don't have any interest… as long as you make love to me right now."
findings.evidenceJa:
「嫌いでも、興味がなくても、もういいよ…
ただ、今だけあたしを抱いてくれたら」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says it no longer matters even if Haruki hates her or lacks interest; the English changes hate to not wanting sex — Her willingness to accept one-sided physical consolation despite his lack of desire remains.
findings.japanese:
「嫌いでも、興味がなくても、もういいよ…
ただ、今だけあたしを抱いてくれたら」
findings.todokanai: "It doesn't matter if you don't want to, or don't have any interest… as long as you make love to me right now."

findings.highlight: If I make love to you, I won't ever be able to let you go!
findings.evidenceJa: 抱きしめたら、二度と離せなくなる！
findings.explanation: Haruki says that if he embraces Kazusa, he will never be able to let her go again. Although the surrounding proposal is sexual, 抱きしめる here is deliberately the emotional act of holding her; the English turns it into intercourse and destroys the hold/let-go parallel.
findings.japanese:
「愛してるって言ったら、
お前が世界で一番になっちまう！
抱きしめたら、二度と離せなくなる！」
findings.todokanai: "If I say that I love you, you'll become the most precious person in the world to me! If I make love to you, I won't ever be able to let you go!"

findings.highlight: from a dwelling heat in my body
findings.evidenceJa: 息遣いでも、しずくの感触でもなく、全身に宿り始めた、病以外の熱量から。
findings.explanation: Haruki can read Kazusa's stronger gaze from the non-fever heat beginning to inhabit her whole body, not merely from breath or tears. The English locates that heat in Haruki's body, reversing whose renewed passion he is sensing.
findings.japanese:
息遣いでも、しずくの感触でもなく、
全身に宿り始めた、病以外の熱量から。
findings.todokanai: Not because of her breaths or the sensation of her tears, but from a dwelling heat in my body.
